faq.a: Aanisah represents Arabic أنيسة (ʾanīsah), the feminine form of أنيس, with senses such as companionable, sociable, or friendly.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aanisah?
faq.a: The recorded form أنيسة is Arabic; this linguistic origin does not prove the history of every individual bearer.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is أنيسة (ʾanīsah).

faq.q: What is the root of Aanisah?
faq.a: The form is associated with the Arabic root أ ن س (ʾ-n-s), linked to familiarity, companionship, and sociability.
Aanisah is used by Muslims as a personal name, but it is a lexical word rather than an exclusively religious title.
This record does not establish Aanisah as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin alone is not evidence of Qur'anic status.

faq.q: What does Aanisah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu script it is written انیسہ. The record glosses it as خوش مزاج، ملنسار، مانوس, though a native-language review is advisable.
The supplied romanization “aa-ni-sah” is approximate; no verified IPA transcription is recorded.

faq.q: Is Aanisah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Aanisah as feminine, consistent with the Arabic form أنيسة; individual naming practices can vary.
